text:
mike: Heads-up — nightly canary started hitting GPU OOMs after the kernel-selection change (tiling_pref enabled). Repro on g4dn with paged-attn heavy traces.

mike: Logs: ```allocator: arena grow from 6GB -> 12GB; blockmgr: failed to allocate block 32768 bytes; runtime: OOM at workspace_reserve()
kv_cache: inflight keys=18, avg_kv_size=1.2MB
```

ana: @mike can you paste the kernel selection flags you flipped? did we switch prefetch and tiling together?

mike: Switched default from stream-first to tiling_pref + prefetch_kv=true in the kernel chooser. No other changes. Batching left at continuous-batching target_tokens=8192.

li: Tiling tends to increase working set fragmentation for small-block allocators — it scatters per-request workspace shapes. Combined with aggressive batching that could bloat the kv cache residency.

carla: Also check sequence length distribution. If we have many long tails, prefetch_kv will pin large KV entries across many slots.

mike: Seq lengths: median 256, 75p 512, 95p ~900. So long tail is real.

perf-bot: perf alert: nightly-tiling experiment -> peak_memory +32%, p99 latency +9%. Regression id: r-tiling-2026-03-17.

ana: Proposed triage plan: 1) roll kernel selection back to stream-first on canary, 2) run microbench with block_size=32k vs 64k to measure fragmentation, 3) enable slab-merge (defrag on threshold) and arena-trim on idle.

li: Agree. Also test lowering target_tokens to 4096 and enable per-workspace token cap so one bursty request can't inflate global batching window. Batching heuristics should consider seq-length variance, not just token budget.

carla: Add a cheap metric: block_reuse_rate histogram (reuses per-block per-minute) and compaction_count. If slab-merge reduces compaction_count but raises CPU by <6% it's probably worth it.

mike: Quick config I'll try locally: ```yaml
kernel_choice: stream-first
batching: { target_tokens: 4096, per_workspace_limit: 2 }
blockmgr: { block_size: 32768, slab_merge_threshold: 0.7, arena_trim_on_idle: true }
kv_cache: prefetch_kv: false
```

ana: Nice. Also add an experiment that toggles block_size and measures average free-run fragmentation: run 10k synthetic requests with mixed seq lengths and report max_contiguous_free, avg_block_reuse.

li: If rollback fixes OOMs, we can reintroduce tiling but with a different workspace sizing policy: limit reserved_ws per-thread and prefer compact-allocate path for small KV footprints.

perf-bot: New experiment scheduled: canary-rollback-tiling at 2187654335. Metrics will stream to #observability.

deploy-bot: Canary deployed to us-east-1 with config id canary-tiling-roll-2187. Link: https://deploys/redwood/canary-2187

mike: Running local membench now. Will post results in ~30m. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

carla: If you see compaction bursts, dump a trace with `BLOCK_DUMP=1` and attach. That helps isolate whether merges are CPU-bound or just metadata churn.

mike: Will do. If rollback doesn't help, next steps: enable eager-evict for low-priority keys, and set a hysteresis window on KV eviction to avoid thrashing.

li: Sounds good — also add a small heap-scan after eviction to catch leaked arenas (we saw a leak in a previous quantization patch).

mike: Update: local membench run (10k requests mixed seq): block_size=32k -> peak 9.8GB, compactions 12; block_size=64k -> peak 11.6GB, compactions 5 but avg_contiguous_free smaller. Initial impression: 32k reduces peak by ~15% at cost of slightly higher compaction count. Posting full numbers shortly.

carla: Great data — looks promising. Once the canary finishes, let's reconvene and decide whether to keep stream-first as default or introduce a new kernel policy that prefers tiling only when median seq < 300.

mike: Ack. I'll drop the detailed CSV into the thread when ready.

perf-bot: Canary finished: memory peak normalized after rollback; tail latency returned to baseline. Final: peak_memory delta -28% vs tiling run.

mike: Closing the loop — rollback prevented OOMs. We'll iterate on a conditional tiling policy and tweak batching heuristics before re-enabling by default.

carla: :rocket: Thanks all.
